title: Solvable radical and centre of a Lie algebra
statement:
For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, its solvable
radical $\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak g)$ is the sum of all solvable
ideals (solvability and ideals as in [def-wf-lie-algebra]), and its centre is

$$
\mathfrak z(\mathfrak g)=\{X\in\mathfrak g:[X,Y]=0\text{ for all }Y\in\mathfrak g\}.
$$

The sum $\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak g)$ is again solvable, and is
therefore the unique largest solvable ideal of $\mathfrak g$.

mathlib_match.how: One Mathlib declaration per clause, specialized to the base field k of def-wf-lie-algebra. LieAlgebra.radical (Solvable.lean:365-366) is sSup of all solvable Lie ideals, which is their sum. LieAlgebra.center (Abelian.lean:286-287) is LieModule.maxTrivSubmodule k L L; LieModule.mem_maxTrivSubmodule (Abelian.lean:173-174) gives x in center iff forall y, [y,x]=0. The one-line rewrite by lie_skew (Basic.lean:179-181) and neg_eq_zero gives the stated forall y, [x,y]=0 condition, in every characteristic. LieAlgebra.radicalIsSolvable (Solvable.lean:369-375) gives the solvability clause, and LieAlgebra.LieIdeal.solvable_iff_le_radical (Solvable.lean:378-380) says that every solvable ideal is contained in the radical. Hence the radical is the unique largest such ideal, uniqueness being antisymmetry. Its IsNoetherian k L hypothesis is inferred: FiniteDimensional (FiniteDimensional/Defs.lean:75-76) abbreviates Module.Finite; DivisionSemiring.isPrincipalIdealRing (PrincipalIdealDomain.lean:72-77) and PrincipalIdealRing.isNoetherianRing (same file:115-117) make the field Noetherian; isNoetherian_of_isNoetherianRing_of_finite (Noetherian/Basic.lean:324-328) gives IsNoetherian k L. No algebraic-closure or characteristic-zero hypothesis is used.
